ratings_why.fun: Picking which carry the back row hangs on is a real decision every turn, and the late game grows hard, but turns 1 to 4 still lean on small +1/+1 floors.
ratings_why.distinct: An 8 over a 7 because its growth is another tribe's growth, and the host is picked by the staggered board itself: no tribe today grows off someone else's carry or gives the back row a job.

verdict_why: The engine and curve are settled; two cards still read two ways and need a wording pass.

points.text: Barley-Sugar Twiner's "its host gains its biggest gain" can read as the Twiner's gain; say "the host's biggest gain this round", and say whether a second Twiner can repeat the first one's repeat.
Adult Ivy "rises with its host's two biggest gains" doesn't say half of each, and the golden climber rule has the same gap; one word fixes both.
13 climbers fight for 3 back slots until Tier 4, so the Tier 4 to 5 shops roll many dead cards; one more front-row climber, or Ivy-clad Ruin a tier lower, would smooth the middle game.
Young Ivy is the only real seed and its value is all borrowed; a second Tier 1 that grows on its own would give the first three turns a shape to play.

Lady Hedera's guest-book shuffle is the best puzzle in the tribe; let her also sign when a new tribe's unit is played in front of her, so the climb to five signatures isn't stuck on a two-tribe board.

standouts.why: Viscum copies every gain in full but drops off the moment he outgrows his host, so the snob limits his own runaway.
Old Man's Beard turns a dead carry into the back row's new front line, which makes losing the host a payoff.
Lady Hedera rewards moving across tribes each turn, a capstone built on behaviour rather than one big number.

weakest.why: Hop Bine pays one gold a turn at best and spends a scarce back slot doing it.
Ivy Bush gives +1/+1 per climber, small even at Tier 2, and asks for climbers you can't place yet.
Dodder Seedling is a plain tempo body that the rest of the tribe never uses.

flags.note: Cousin Dodder takes a quarter of the biggest enemy on every attack, permanently; with Viscum or Twiner copying the takes it climbs very fast late, though it draws from the enemy, not itself.
Golden Viscum doubles every host gain; on a golden Ooze carry he is capped only by the host's own size.
"its biggest gain" can mean the Twiner's or the host's.
